  • Managed service lifecycle problems: relaunch can fail when a previous background service has not exited (#54267).
  • Provider/model configuration mismatches: missing Global privacy setting for DeepSeek V4 Flash (#50155), empty model picker (#54092), and incorrect Copilot URL (#45302).
  • Retry/backoff is not configurable: hardcoded retry limits abort transient provider errors too early (#43596).
  • TUI/desktop polish gaps: Thai combining-mark width handling (#49348), close-button placement (#54438), file attachment flow (#54743), plugin/MCP input readability (#54703), and bash coloring (#54700/#54701).
  • MCP/request resource pressure: MCP discovery can consume slow-request slots and leave discovery-only connections open (#53050, #53046).
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-10-12

Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but issue traffic was heavy: 50 issues were updated, dominated by OpenAI/ChatGPT authentication and quota-state bugs plus a cluster of 1.1.0 regressions in codemode and the TUI. On the PR side, the maintainers closed out several long-standing extension-lifecycle fixes — notably before_agent_start now fires for runs started by custom messages (#10739) — and shipped the OpenRouter per-key model filtering requested in #10353. The only open PR is #10795, an Anthropic tool-result image fix.

Hot Issues

  1. #4945 — openai-codex Connection Reliability Issues (OPEN, inprogress, 82 comments, 35 👍) The community's hottest thread by a wide margin. gpt-5.5 over openai-codex intermittently hangs the interactive TUI on Working... with no streamed text, no tool call, and no error; the only escape is Esc, which logs an aborted turn. High like count signals this is widely reproduced, not an edge case.

  2. #10480 — Direct openai connection not recognising manual usage limit reset (OPEN, 18 comments) Banked ChatGPT Pro resets are ignored on the direct OpenAI connection, leaving users locked out until they /logout and re-login via openai-codex. A painful billing/entitlement correctness bug with a known workaround.

  3. #10605 — ChatGPT/OpenAI OAuth 403 issue (OPEN, 10 comments, 1 👍) Plus-tier users hit subscription_sharing_user_not_eligible after logout/login. Same family as #10480 and likely part of a broader credential/entitlement state problem.

  4. #7553 — Configurable thinking level/model for compaction (OPEN, inprogress/to-discuss, 10 comments, 3 👍) Compaction unconditionally inherits the session thinking level, so summarization burns the same reasoning budget as normal turns. A well-scoped, repeatedly requested knob for users running auto-compaction on reasoning models.

  5. #10267 — Prompt text from before_agent_start dropped on non-user-prompt runs (CLOSED, p0, 9 comments, 4 👍) Marked P0 because the drop forces re-billing of the whole prompt on background-task notifications, plan-mode continues, retries, and resumes. Fixed by #10739.

  6. #5581 — pi.sendMessage() with triggerTurn: true bypasses before_agent_start (CLOSED, 9 comments, 4 👍) The root cause behind a family of extension bugs: the agent loop was kicked via _runAgentPrompt directly, skipping emitBeforeAgentStart and silently changing the system prompt mid-run.

  7. #9602 — Compaction can overflow by including thinking messages omitted from earlier requests (OPEN, 9 comments) With local Qwen3.8 via llama.cpp, thinking content excluded from prior requests still counts toward compaction, causing overflow. Another entry in the growing compaction-correctness backlog.

  8. #10645 — resizeImage resolves null in compiled Bun executables (OPEN, inprogress, 6 comments) Standalone binaries from v0.87.1/v1.0.4 silently drop all image attachments because resizeImage fails under Bun compilation. A functional regression for RPC integrators, with clean reproduction via a fake gateway.

  9. #10821 — Terminal resize freezes the UI with long sessions (CLOSED, 2 comments) Every resize frame synchronously re-lays out the entire transcript; severely degrades on Windows Terminal/VS Code terminals. A 1.1.0-era TUI performance regression.

  10. #10678 — codemode joinAdjacentText is quadratic (CLOSED, 3 comments, 1 👍) Introduced in 1.1.0: scripts calling text() tens of thousands of times block the host thread because joining runs synchronously with quadratic cost. Fast turnaround on the fix, but a notable release-quality miss.

Key PR Progress

  1. #10739 — emit before_agent_start for runs started by custom messages (CLOSED) Closes out #5581 and #10267: next-turn refresh no longer patches away handler-added prompt sections, preserving system-prompt stability and provider prompt caching.

  2. #10672 — list only the OpenRouter models a key may use (CLOSED) Combines the catalog with GET /models/user, keeping context size, max output, and pricing from the authenticated response. Implements #10353.

  3. #10820 — send x-opencode-session by endpoint, not provider id (CLOSED) Generalizes #9326: any provider routed to OpenCode zen endpoints now gets the per-conversation routing header, avoiding 400 MissingSessionID.

  4. #10819 — use registerToolRenderer in the minimal-mode example (CLOSED) Docs fix with real consequences: re-registering built-ins with pi.registerTool({...}) replaced execute entirely, silently breaking extensions that reroute built-in tool execution.

  5. #10813 — preserve client-loaded Anthropic tool references (CLOSED) Keeps tool references supplied by the client intact through the Anthropic provider path.

  6. #10774 — enable kitty images in herdr (CLOSED) Reverts an unintended 1.1.0 regression where #10573 returned images: null for herdr panes despite herdr supporting the kitty graphics protocol.

  7. #10810 — support override colorFn options in CompactionStatusIndicator (CLOSED) Fixes #10809; aligns the compaction indicator with WorkingIndicator for themes that don't set borderColor.

  8. #10805 — support extension session cwd (CLOSED) Adds cwd to ctx.newSession() and cwdOverride to ctx.switchSession(), completing the git-worktree workflow extensions could already script via pi.exec.

  9. #10751 — use pi.dev configuration schemas (CLOSED) Makes pi.dev schema endpoints the canonical $id values for generated settings, models, keybindings, and theme schemas, and adopts the published theme schema in built-ins/examples.

  10. #10795 — drop images from Anthropic error tool results (OPEN) The only PR still open; fixes #10794 by stripping images from Anthropic error tool results, with before/after session traces attached.

Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #10808 — Pippa, a native Mac interface for everyday Pi tasks (1 👍) A free, MIT-licensed Swift macOS app that talks to Pi over pi --mode rpc, letting non-terminal users drop a letter or folder onto a floating pill and pick a task. Local models run through llama.cpp, with Mac integrations layered on top; the author is recruiting testers.

Feature Request Trends

  • Compaction control and correctness: the single strongest theme across the window. Requests span a dedicated thinking level/model for compaction (#7553), overflow from thinking messages (#9602), abort semantics during pre-prompt compaction (#10289), and transport settings not applying to summary requests (#10781).
  • Provider entitlement and model discovery: users want Pi's UI to reflect real account state rather than the static catalog — per-key OpenRouter model filtering (#10353), honoring ChatGPT usage resets (#10480), and warning instead of silently falling back when a saved default model disappears (#10812).
  • Extension lifecycle guarantees: consistent before_agent_start semantics (#5581, #10267, #10639), safe renderer overrides (#10819), and session cwd control for worktree flows (#10805).
  • Tool/MCP declaration fidelity: prompt sections must match the tools actually exposed — MCP servers removed by --no-tools/--exclude-tools are still advertised (#10635), codemode drops input constraints like minimum/maximum/default (#10707), and Anthropic thinking.display: "updates" is requested (#10804).
  • Headless/unattended agent robustness: explicit continuation paths for max-token stops (#10799), generic classifier model support on custom providers (#10791), and cheaper image handling via ChatGPT file_id references (#8617).

Developer Pain Points

  • Provider connectivity and account state are the top recurring frustration. Silent TUI hangs on openai-codex (#4945) and 403/quota-state mismatches (#10480, #10605) force logins, workarounds, and aborted turns.
  • Silent failures over loud errors. Dropped RPC prompts acknowledged with success: true (#10606), skipped before_agent_start calls (#10639), ignored default models (#10812), and output-limit stops that settle without notice (#10799) all cost debugging time because nothing surfaces.
  • 1.1.0 regression cluster. Quadratic codemode text joining (#10678), synchronous full-transcript relayout on resize (#10821), and broken herdr inline images (#10774) suggest release-testing gaps around TUI and codemode paths.
  • Prompt-cache and cost regressions from lifecycle bugs. Re-billing entire prompts when contributed prompt text is dropped (#10267) and mid-run system-prompt changes that break provider caches (#10739) directly hit users' wallets.
  • Platform-specific sharp edges. Windows auth lock acquisition failing on transient EPERM (#10801), orphaned Playwright Chrome processes after bash timeouts on macOS (#10797), mouse-wheel target confusion under Windows + Zellij (#9656), and broken image attachments in compiled Bun binaries (#10645) keep platform coverage on the critical path.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-10-12

Data source: github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code

1. Today's Highlights

Release activity centers on the v0.25.1 line, with matching SDK (TypeScript v0.1.19) and Desktop (v0.25.1) artifacts. The dominant engineering theme remains the Managed Agent architecture (durable Sessions, writer fencing/takeover, team messaging, L4 Shell/MCP lifecycle), which continues to drive the majority of high-traffic issues and PRs. Meanwhile, a cluster of new reports around UTF-8 BOM config files silently failing and CI/release-tooling reliability (Flyway ordering, CVE audit, duplicated release notes) highlights growing friction in configuration robustness and automation.

2. Releases

Release Notes
v0.25.1 Stable CLI release. Auto-generated notes; the only substantive feature line references restoring a text-only connection and validated session/workspace route after Android Activity recreation. Full change list is not populated in the notes.
v0.25.1-nightly.20261011.01d3e6d81a Nightly carrying fix(managed-agent): connector and broker robustness (#13330) plus additional managed-agent work.
sdk-typescript-v0.1.19 Bundles CLI version 0.25.1 (built from the same source branch/ref as the SDK). Release body also references bundled CLI 0.25.0, suggesting stale/duplicated note generation.
desktop-v0.25.1 Desktop release includes fix(serve): preserve session creation failure diagnostics (#12331) and feat(sdk-java): Add managed runtime work; ships .deb (amd64/arm64) and AppImage artifacts.

⚠️ Note: Release notes for this window appear partially duplicative — directly related to open issue #13925.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #12380 — Proposal(serve): Define Managed Agent dual-path architecture and staged delivery (56 comments, OPEN) The umbrella design for keeping the TypeScript agent loop while decoupling inference from tool-environment provisioning, with durable Session ownership, Workspace bindings, recoverable tool executions, and a stable Web Shell surface. It is the single most-discussed issue in the repo and the parent of most managed-agent workstreams (Stages G, H3, H4).

  2. #13078 — Daily dependency CVE audit failed (18 comments, OPEN) A scheduled security audit job is failing repeatedly, with maintainers investigating whether it is a genuine high-severity finding or npm audit endpoint instability. High community attention because it gates supply-chain hygiene.

  3. #12952 — Stage G: authoritative Session history, writer fencing and takeover (8 comments, OPEN) Defines the slices and exit checks for externalizing Session history/checkpoints and proving writer fencing before removing owner affinity. This is the architectural hinge for multi-writer/hosted sessions.

  4. #13680 — [P1] Desktop Linux vendored ripgrep rewritten post-link, SIGSEGVs on startup probe (4 comments, OPEN) The x64-linux rg binary has an injected DT_RUNPATH $ORIGIN and moved ELF program headers, crashing every startup probe. The only P1 in this window — a hard blocker for Linux desktop users.

  5. #13807 — "ERROR 500 An unsupported generation guide was used" with macOS Foundation Models as Fast Model (6 comments, OPEN) Works for tool summaries but fails on the fast-model path when using fm serve via an openai:system… provider string. Points at provider/routing edge cases for local OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

  6. #13924 — Publish Qwen Code Desktop on Flathub with a working update channel (5 comments, OPEN) Requests Flathub distribution so Linux app stores (e.g., Mint Software Manager) can list the app and provide updates. Builds on the already-shipping .deb/AppImage artifacts.

  7. #13875 — [H4f] Parent close waits for running child Turn instead of stopping it (4 comments, OPEN) Cancel-then-close leaves child Sessions executing. A correctness gap in multi-agent lifecycle semantics that directly affects cancellation guarantees.

  8. #13922 — Flyway migrations numbered below main's newest pass both version checks (4 comments, OPEN) Both uniqueness gates only check for duplicates, not ordering, so upgraded databases can refuse to start. Notable because it allows a broken migration to merge green.

  9. #13944 / #13943 — UTF-8 BOM config files silently skipped (3 comments each, OPEN) A .toml custom command file with a BOM is dropped (Unknown character "65279"), and a BOM-prefixed .lsp.json causes the entire file to be discarded with only a debug log — so no LSP servers start and users see no error. Related: #13710 closed for Claude MCP import.

  10. #13925 — Release notes duplicate PRs released in previous releases (3 comments, OPEN) Desktop release notes are accreting entries instead of scoping to the current release — a visible trust issue for downstream users tracking what actually shipped.

Also worth tracking: #13951 (CI checkout pack has 1 unresolved delta), #13920 (CJK teammate names collapse in sanitizeName), #13942 (multi-provider, same model ID switching friction), #13930 (H3 held-Runtime drain follow-ups).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #13940 — feat(managed-agent): Java mirror of managed-event-envelope contract (MQ2a) First sub-slice of the EventTransport MQ2 phase: a Java mirror of the frozen managed-event-envelope/1 contract plus a fixture consumer proving cross-language parity.

  2. #13950 — feat(mods): Add tool interception and permission checks (PR3a) Adds tool.call / tool.check hooks to opt-in Mods: rewrite arguments, refuse calls, return synthetic JSON, and inspect/replace native tool results — with every next re-entering native validation, hooks, and permissions.

  3. #13952 — feat(web-shell): Bridge trajectory history and live lifecycle state Connects historical trajectory windows to bounded request/tool lifecycle state via the session subscription; reconnects preserve page, selection, filters, and scroll position.

  4. #13878 — feat(web-shell): Add workspace file browser and previews A Files action in the right panel with full-width workspace tree, Markdown/HTML/image rendering, read-only source inspection, and resizable/removable tree.

  5. #13957 — fix(cli): Preserve Markdown in height-bounded tool results Restores Markdown formatting in completed CLI tool results while keeping terminal-height limits, truncation cues, and expansion — with height accounting for wrapping, list markers, code gutters, and tables.

  6. #13777 — feat(managed-agent): Recover Hosted G3 parked turns Implements recovery for G3 parked turns on the Hosted stack, a key durability step toward Stage G exit criteria.

  7. #13931 — feat(managed-agent): L4 Shell and MCP session lifecycle Adds durable close/delete for hosted-workspace-shell/1 and hosted-workspace-mcp/1, settling business effects and SessionEnd/SessionDelete hooks exactly once before detaching the writer.

  8. #13955 — feat(managed-agent): Member-to-member messages ride the session_command channel (H4e-b3c) Team members can message each other end-to-end over a durable command channel with no model turn spinning up on the lead. Companion: #13928 (member board tools).

  9. #13815 — fix(managed-agent): Numeric parity and family-list hoisting with end-to-end admission and wedge witnesses Fixes the capture-publication reserve refusing background Shell/Monitor payloads, and adds end-to-end admission tests plus wedge witnesses after review churn. (#13918 addresses the related tenant-wide InnoDB lock blast radius.)

  10. #13954 — fix(ci): Enforce Flyway migration ordering Both Flyway gates now reject newly added versions that are not strictly greater than the highest published version across scanned modules and SQL/Java locations — directly closing the gap from #13922.

Also notable: #13654 (async tool-publication verification), #13642 (bounded JDBC history retention), #13929 (Monitor auto-stop exit evidence), #13938 (closed — Web Shell voice feedback localization), #13335 (closed — config/API surface hygiene).

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window. Section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Managed Agent / multi-agent platform (dominant): durable Session history and ownership, writer fencing and takeover, workspace bindings, recoverable/verified tool executions, parent-child lifecycle correctness, team member-to-member messaging and shared boards, and durable Shell/MCP session lifecycle. See #12380, #12952, #13875, #13271.
  • Linux / platform distribution: Flathub listing with a working update channel, alongside existing .deb and AppImage targets. See #13924.
  • Web Shell ergonomics: workspace/project pinning in the sidebar (#12444, with duplicate #13888 already closed), file browsing and previews, localized and dismissible voice feedback.
  • Model provider flexibility: multiple providers serving the same model ID with distinguishable names and quick switching (#13942); documented local/OpenAI-compatible providers such as Rapid-MLX (#13934); macOS Foundation Models as a fast model (#13807).
  • Configuration robustness: graceful handling of UTF-8 BOM and other encoding quirks across TOML, JSON, LSP, and imported Claude MCP configs (#13944, #13943, #13710).
  • CI/CD and release tooling reliability: CVE audit stability, migration ordering enforcement, release-note deduplication, and more accurate review-automation parsing (#13078, #13922, #13925, #13735).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Silent failures on malformed config. BOM-prefixed .toml, .lsp.json, and imported Claude configs are discarded with only debug-level logging, producing confusing symptoms (missing slash commands, "No LSP servers configured," no diagnostics). Multiple independent reporters in one window suggest an encoding-hardening sweep is warranted.
  • CI gates that pass when they shouldn't. The Flyway checks permitted out-of-order migrations, the dependency CVE audit job is chronically failing, and integration lanes hit Git-level errors (pack has 1 unresolved delta) — eroding confidence in green builds.
  • Release-notes accuracy. Duplicated PR entries across Desktop releases make it hard for users to know what actually shipped; the v0.25.1 notes are similarly under-populated.
  • Lifecycle correctness in multi-agent flows. Parent close that waits rather than stops child turns, and recovery-blocked sessions wedging unrelated sessions via tenant-wide locks, are high-impact reliability concerns.
  • Internationalization edge cases. CJK teammate names collapsing to empty in sanitizeName forces model-invented pinyin fallbacks — a correctness issue for non-English users adopting Agent Teams.
  • Token/context accounting gaps. Compaction sizing against an inferred window instead of the server-reported ceiling (#13432, now closed) reflects recurring sensitivity around context-limit behavior.
  • Multi-provider model switching friction. Users must change providers in the CLI to reach the same model served by different vendors; the absence of per-provider aliasing is a repeated usability complaint.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-10-12

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-12 08:27 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-12

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 依然非常活跃：过去 24 小时内共有 500 个 issue 更新（357 个打开/活跃，143 个已关闭），另有 500 个 PR 更新（363 个打开，137 个已合并/关闭），并发布了两个新版本。最新版本几乎全部聚焦于更新可靠性：v2026.10.2 修复了从稳定版 2026.10.1 进行干净的原地升级，v2026.10.5-beta.1 强化了跨设备、文件系统、Windows 提权以及中断激活场景下的更新。然而，issue 跟踪器显示仍持续存在高严重级稳定性问题，尤其是内存泄漏、僵尸进程、更新失败、会话状态丢失，以及插件捕获性能回退。因此项目健康状况喜忧参半：维护吞吐量很高，但未解决的 P0/P1 issue 仍在影响生产部署，尤其是在 Windows、npm 全局安装，以及复杂的容器/文件系统环境下。

2. 版本发布

v2026.10.2

链接：https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.2

发布说明要点：

  • 从稳定版 2026.10.1 进行的首次升级现在可以顺利完成。
  • 成功的原地更新不再以错误告终。
  • Windows、克隆文件系统以及私有 Node 的更新路径现在能够完成，而不是卡住或回滚。
  • 引用修复：#168849、#169031。

v2026.10.5-beta.1

链接：https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.5-beta.1

发布说明要点：

  • 在跨设备、文件系统、Windows 提权以及中断激活场景下实现更安全的更新。
  • 可从过期租约或已变更证据中恢复，而不是让安装陷入停滞或阻止后续更新。
  • 引用修复：#164636、#164769、#165257、#165863，另有一个被截断的引用。

破坏性变更 / 迁移说明： 提供的发布说明未提及明确的破坏性变更。主要迁移信号是更新路径的韧性得到改善，这应能减少升级失败时的手动恢复。尽管如此，许多未关闭的 issue 仍报告在 npm 全局、Windows、LXC 以及 Windows 多代理安装中出现更新失败，因此运维人员在重大升级前仍应备份状态。

3. 项目进展

  • 今日合并/关闭的 PR： 137 个。
  • 今日关闭的 issue： 143 个。

已关闭的 issue 表明修复已在多个领域落地：

  • 更新可靠性： #164113 — 在非特权 LXC 中，更新在 updater-runtime-retention 处因 FICLONE EPERM 失败；已通过可排队修复关闭。链接：https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164113
  • 包恢复： #167506 — 删除的临时交接数据库阻塞了包恢复和后续更新；已关闭。链接：https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/167506
  • 会话状态： #69118 — 由于 groupIntro 漂移，Claude CLI 会话在群组频道中每轮都会重置；已作为已修复关闭。链接：https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/69118
  • 模型请求序列化： #123265 — role:"custom" 运行时上下文载体在每个请求中都被序列化为末尾的 user 消息；已关闭。链接：https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123265
  • 内存/CPU 饱和： #136175 — 完整的本地内存重建索引使 CPU 饱和并阻塞诊断；已关闭。链接：https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/136175
  • 子代理幂等性： #37446 — 子代理超时恢复创建了重复的 API 提交；已关闭。链接：https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/37446

大量开放 PR 活动由维护者 steipete 推动，重点在于架构简化以及将同步 SQLite 工作移出 Gateway 线程：

  • #169648 — 简化状态与进程 worker 生命周期。https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169648
  • #169584 — 通过 worker 准备执行策略。https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169584
  • #169580 — 将 Gateway 状态消费者迁至现有 worker。https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169580
  • #169566 — 通过 worker 路由会话 fork、读取和清理。https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169566
  • #169735 — 避免冗余的提醒和会话快照 SQL。https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169735
  • #169707 — 减少 Control UI 冷加载聊天渲染。https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169707
  • #169709 — 减少空闲 Gateway 事件循环采样工作。https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169709

还有一个重要的开放 P1 PR，旨在实现更安全的更新：

  • #144005 —“在迁移前备份状态，并在回滚时恢复。”仍处于打开状态，标记为 needs proof，范围较大。https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144005

4. 社区热点

按评论数排序的最活跃 issue：

  1. #91588 — P0 Gateway 内存泄漏（38 条评论）
    RSS 在数天内从约 350 MB 增长到 15.5 GB，导致反复 OOM 崩溃。没有新的修复 PR。
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91588

  2. #159356 — llama.cpp 管理器报告就绪，但 embedding 子进程已退出（26 条评论）
    Embedding 请求返回 HTTP 500“Failed to read connection”；严重级为 P2，但会影响会话状态和崩溃循环。
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159356

  3. #97616 — P1 未回收的 hook/tool 子进程（18 条评论）
    主 openclaw 进程下僵尸进程累积，导致运行时性能下降。
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97616

  4. #148707 — P1 回复因“no active tool authority snapshot”而丢失（18 条评论）

7. 用户反馈摘要

  • 对稳定性的严重不满： 用户报告 OOM 崩溃、内存泄漏、僵尸进程、SQLite 损坏以及 gateway 挂起，使部署无法使用（#91588、#155191、#97616、#126821、#167652）。
  • 更新之痛普遍存在： openclaw update 在 npm 全局安装、Windows、LXC 容器和克隆文件系统上失败，而直接 npm 安装往往可以成功（#156112、#168955、#167652、#164113、#167506）。
  • 性能与硬件担忧： 插件源码捕获每条命令、每次 Gateway 启动都会重写数 GB 数据，导致 SSD 磨损和数分钟的事件循环阻塞（#160959、#157989）。
  • 消息丢失和会话连续性至关重要： 用户在负载或重连下丢失回复、WhatsApp 群组消息、Telegram 回调和会话状态（#148707、#107244、#126950、#54488）。
  • 平台特定摩擦： Windows 用户面临工具输出为空、启动缓慢、挂起和 DataCloneError；iOS 用户在启用 reasoning/tool activity 时出现卡顿（#105528、#166894、#158788、#124759）。
  • 维护者响应速度令人担忧： 许多高影响 issue 被标记为 needs-maintainer-review 或 needs-product-decision，并持续打开数周或数月。
  • 一位用户放弃了部署： #88087 记录了 DigitalOcean droplet 上长时间运行后台任务的糟糕 UX 以及静默 cron 唤醒失败，最终导致用户将其拆除。https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/88087
  • 积极信号： 项目非常活跃，版本发布频繁，今天还关闭了若干长期存在的 issue，包括更新和会话状态修复。用户继续提供包含环境细节的详细报告。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告——个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态系统

时间窗口： 2026-10-11 → 2026-10-12 | 项目： OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw

方法说明： 活跃度数据直接取自各项目的 24 小时摘要。健康度评分为分析师指定的综合评分（1–10），权衡活跃吞吐量、关闭率、发布节奏、关键积压严重程度和社区参与度——它们不是厂商或 GitHub 提供的指标。OpenClaw 的 Issue/PR 数量似乎触及 API 的 500 条上限，应理解为“≥500”。

1. 生态系统概览

个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态正在功能上趋同，结构上分化。几乎每个活跃项目都在独立重建同一核心栈——Gateway、插件/扩展运行时、MCP 工具管线、记忆/压缩层、多渠道入口以及提供商无关的模型路由——但在语言、打包方式和目标用户押注上差异巨大。五个项目共同的主导未解问题不是能力，而是运行可靠性：安装/更新脆弱性、Gateway 资源泄漏、会话持久性和插件沙箱成本出现在每个积压清单中，而参与度最高的社区线程是生产事故报告，而非功能请求。第二个跨领域约束是维护者审查带宽：QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 的贡献者供给健康，但合并延迟——而非想法稀缺——才是约束瓶颈。

2. 活跃度对比

项目 Issue（24 小时） PR（24 小时） 发布状态 健康度评分
OpenClaw 约 500 条更新（357 条开启/活跃，143 条关闭 · 28.6%） 约 500 条更新（363 条开启，137 条合并/关闭 · 27.4%） 2 个版本： v2026.10.2（稳定版，更新修复），v2026.10.5-beta.1 6.5 / 10 — 好坏参半
Hermes Agent 50 条更新（10 条关闭 · 20%） 50 条更新（18 条合并/关闭 · 36%） v0.21.7 补丁（汇总约 204 个 PR） 8.0 / 10 — 强劲
IronClaw 0 7 条更新（3 条合并，4 条开启）——全部为 dependabot 无 6.0 / 10 — 安静/稳定
QwenPaw 13 条触及（至少 1 条关闭，包括 #7311） 23 条更新（13 条合并/关闭 · 57%，10 条开启） 无 7.0 / 10 — 流程良好，发布承压
ZeroClaw 16 条触及（0 条关闭） 45 条更新（2 条关闭 · 4.4%，43 条开启） 无 5.0 / 10 — 受审查瓶颈制约

解读表格： OpenClaw 的原始吞吐量约为最接近同行的 10 倍，比 IronClaw 高出两个数量级，但其关闭率（约 27–29%）落后于 Hermes 和 QwenPaw，因为流入量巨大。ZeroClaw 表现出相反的病理——贡献者流入高，但 合并:开启比为 2:43——表明瓶颈在审查而非需求。QwenPaw 的 57% PR 关闭率是这一组中最健康的，得益于有意识地清理数月积压，尽管已有一批合并修复排队，却未发布任何版本。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

规模优势具有决定性，但也是一把双刃剑。 OpenClaw 在 24 小时内 Issue+PR 合计约 1,000 次触及，令 Hermes（约 100）、QwenPaw（约 36）、ZeroClaw（约 61）和 IronClaw（约 7）相形见绌。它占据事实上的“核心参考”地位，拥有生态中最广的平台覆盖面：Windows、macOS、iOS、WSL2、LXC、Docker、npm-global、克隆文件系统以及多 Agent Windows 安装都出现在其跟踪器中。

与同行的技术路径对比：

维度 OpenClaw 同行对比
运行时 Node/TS 单体 Gateway + 同步 SQLite 状态 ZeroClaw/IronClaw 为 Rust；Hermes 为 Python + 桌面外壳
进行中的重构 通过 worker 将 SQLite/状态工作移出 Gateway 线程（steipete PR 链 #169648/#169580/#169566） ZeroClaw 通过运行时/Gateway 分离追求等效目标（v0.9.0 RFC #7432）
插件模型 外部插件的源码捕获（每个 CLI 命令重写 1.1–1.4 GB，每次 Gateway 启动约 6.5 GB——#157989） IronClaw/ZeroClaw 使用 WASM 沙箱；QwenPaw 转向子进程隔离通道（#8187）
会话模型 会话泳道 + 工具权限快照（#148707 回复丢失回归的来源） Hermes 使用带空闲回收器的桌面后端池；ZeroClaw 追求持久化对等 Agent 轮次（#9597）

社区规模对比： OpenClaw 是唯一一个跟踪器因 API 限制而饱和的项目。Hermes 是可信的第二梯队。QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 拥有积极参与、技术成熟但规模小得多的用户基础。IronClaw 在窗口期内显示 零社区活动。

同行胜过它之处： OpenClaw 最关键的缺陷已经陈旧——P0 Gateway 内存泄漏（#91588）自 2026-06-09 起一直开启，有 38 条评论且没有修复 PR，P0 SQLite 损坏（#126821）自 2026-08-20 起也是如此。Hermes 和 QwenPaw 今天 关闭了相对严重的问题。OpenClaw 的问题总体上不是响应能力，而是在聚焦更新的发布工作中对长期存续 P0 的分诊优先级排序。

4. 共同技术关注领域

这些需求独立出现在 三个或更多 项目中——有力证明这是真正的生态系统级需求，而非单项目偏好。

5. 差异化分析

目标用户 高级用户、自托管者、集成者 消费级桌面用户、小团队 Rust/基础设施开发者 自托管运维者、CJK/HarmonyOS 社区 高级多 Agent 构建者

架构断层线： 基于 Rust 的项目（IronClaw、ZeroClaw）正趋同于将 WASM 沙箱 + 能力边界 作为安全原语，而 JS/Python 项目（OpenClaw、Hermes）仍在管理 进程级隔离和源码捕获成本。OpenClaw 的插件模型是生态中已知最大的效率负债；Rust 项目在这一维度上实际上领先一代。

6. 社区势能与成熟度

第一梯队——超大规模、容量受限： OpenClaw。 生态中速度最高，但处于应对 P0 积压的被动模式。发布最快（24 小时内 2 个），但发布一直狭隘地聚焦更新，而内存/进程泄漏持续数月。

第二梯队——积极稳定并持续发布： Hermes Agent。 最均衡的画像：高吞吐量、实际发布了一个版本、关闭了有意义的安全和生命周期问题（#25793、#105239、#127450），以及一波协调进行中的修复（压缩重试、Windows 状态探测、TUI 锁定）。当前健康度与规模之比最佳。

第三梯队——正在改善但发布匮乏： QwenPaw。 贡献流强劲（57% PR 关闭率），积极清理 6 个月前的 PR 积压，并有高质量社区报告——但在 v2.2.x 回归累积（#8173、#8179、#8175）时 没有发布版本。最高杠杆的单一行动是发布一个版本。

第三梯队 b——重设计、受审查瓶颈制约： ZeroClaw。 六个同时进行的高风险 RFC，架构上雄心勃勃，深度参与的高级用户——但 4.4% 的 PR 关闭率 和一个停滞 50 天的 wasm 相关 PR（#7834 相关链）。更多是在 设计 上迭代，而非 代码。

第四梯队——安静维护： IronClaw。 零 Issue、零人工贡献、仅 dependabot 活动。要么是成熟/冻结的代码库，要么是休眠信号——从本次快照无法判断。

快速迭代： OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw。稳定中： Hermes、QwenPaw。设计中： ZeroClaw。静止： IronClaw。

7. 趋势信号

1. 可靠性就是产品，而不是功能。 在全部五个项目中，评论最多的条目都是事件报告：内存泄漏、FD 耗尽、僵尸进程、静默数据损坏。对开发者而言： 资源治理（RSS、FD、子进程）、原子状态和崩溃恢复如今是采用的基本门槛——而不是路线图事项。

2. 更新/安装正在成为一等子系统。 跨平台提权语义、失败回滚和迁移前备份独立出现在 OpenClaw（PR #144005）、Hermes（#126860）和 QwenPaw（#8179）中。对开发者而言： 从第一天起就以原子性和权限边界意识设计更新路径；它是用户流失的前三大来源之一。

3. 插件沙箱正在转向 WASM 和进程隔离。 IronClaw（wasmtime）、ZeroClaw（WASM 托管链）和 QwenPaw（#8187 子进程隔离）都在远离进程内插件执行。OpenClaw 每个命令 GB 级的源码捕获是一个警示性反例。对开发者而言： 在插件 API 稳定之前选择隔离边界——事后改造代价高昂。

4. 记忆/上下文管理是正确性的新前沿。 压缩、上下文溢出恢复、token 预算和 RAG 语料库在五个项目中都出现。关键的是，用户抱怨的故障模式是 静默且破坏性的——QwenPaw 的二进制损坏（#8179）、ZeroClaw 的默认配置记忆隐藏（#11655）、Hermes 不透明的 /memory approve all（#136738）。

5. 静默失败是被提及最多的单一不满模式。 QwenPaw（#8173、#8175、#8179）、OpenClaw（#159356 embedding 子进程在“ready”时退出）和 Hermes（#135522 静默拒绝审批）都出现相同表述：“没有日志，没有错误。” 对开发者而言： 可调试性和显式失败暴露面是竞争性功能，尤其对自托管运维者而言。

6. 协议互操作性正围绕 MCP 和 A2A 整合。 MCP 现在在 OpenClaw、Hermes 和 QwenPaw 中被默认假定；A2A 是 ZeroClaw 的战略押注（#11254）。对开发者而言： 针对这些协议构建工具和 Agent 接口，而不是定制传输格式——预期寿命更长。

7. 多 Agent 编排正在从实验走向产品。 Kanban worker（Hermes）、子 Agent 幂等性（OpenClaw）、worker 容器（QwenPaw）以及 swarms/Dark Factory（ZeroClaw）表明用户正在超越单 Agent 拓扑，需要生命周期、隔离和策略继承原语。

8. 提供商怪癖仍是未被抽象掉的成本。 DeepSeek、Z.AI、Gemini、claude-cli、Codex 和自定义前缀提供商各自产生项目特定 bug。对开发者而言： 假定提供商异质性是永久的；将模型路由、token 限制默认值和凭据路径视为可配置表面，而非常量。

9. 审查带宽，而非贡献者供给，是生态系统的约束瓶颈。 OpenClaw（维护者标记 needs-maintainer-review）、QwenPaw（约 6 个月的 PR 延迟，现在正在清理）和 ZeroClaw（2:43 合并比）都表现出相同病理。

10. 成本和硬件外部性正在成为 UX 关注点。 OpenClaw 每次启动约 6.5 GB 的插件捕获导致 SSD 磨损（#157989），这是一个早期信号：对于长时间运行的 Agent 部署，资源效率正在进入面向用户的价值主张。

#1977, #2783, #2520 各约 200 天（现已关闭） 解决值得欢迎，但有意义的健壮性 PR 约 6 个月延迟是审查吞吐量红旗，值得从结构上解决。

积压健康度结论： 项目今天显然正在处理积压，但 #1977/#2783/#2520/#4707 的多月延迟表明瓶颈是维护者审查能力，而非贡献者供给。结合 24 小时内无发布以及一批开放的 v2.2.x 回归，最高杠杆的行动是切出一个版本，发布刚合并的修复。

摘要是根据截至 2026-10-12 的 24 小时窗口内的 GitHub 活动数据生成的。源数据中 PR 的评论数不可用（undefined）；因此 PR 按新近度和范围标签排序。

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw 项目简报 — 2026-10-12

1. 今日概览

ZeroClaw 在 2026-10-12 展现出高速度、低吞吐的工程活动：过去 24 小时内有 45 个 PR 和 16 个 issue 被触及，但仅关闭了 2 个 PR、0 个 issue，且没有新版本发布。项目正处于设计密集型阶段，同时有六个高风险 RFC 处于开启状态，涵盖 A2A 协议 crate、临时智能体集群、RAG/知识语料库、提供商路由以及运行时/网关分离——其中大多数在等待维护者审查或作者处理。来自少量贡献者（IftekharUddin、JordanTheJet、NiuBlibing）的大量堆叠 PR 工作，正在推动插件/WASM 托管、能力边界重构与网关加固，但几乎全部仍处于开启且未合并状态。与此同时，面向用户的缺陷报告持续出现（配对码、Web 聊天焦点、记忆整合），表明真实世界的上手摩擦正在以快于解决的速度被提交。整体健康度：贡献者参与度高、路线图方向清晰，但合并积压不断扩大，已接受的追踪项/RFC 与已交付代码之间存在显著差距。

2. 版本发布

无。 过去 24 小时没有新版本发布。若干开启中的 PR 带有 release:v0.8.6 和 release:v0.9.0 标签，表明两条版本线仍在推进：

  • #7432 — Phase 2 运行时工作（v0.8.6）与 Phase 3 网关分离（v0.9.0）的追踪项
  • #11187、#11261、#11262、#11347 — 均标记为 v0.8.6

今日无需报告破坏性变更或迁移说明。

3. 项目进展

24 小时窗口内仅合并/关闭了 2 个 PR，而仍有 43 个开启——比例明显失衡。

今日关闭：

  • #11531 [CLOSED] — fix(tunnel): report the URL tailscale actually serves the gateway on。修复了一个真实的误报缺陷：网关对外声明 https://<host>:<local_port>，而 Tailscale 实际上在 443 端口提供 HTTPS。改动很小（size:XS），来自一位杰出贡献者。

推进中但尚未合并（高信号集群）：

  • 插件/WASM 基础设施栈 — #11261、#11262、#11347、#11309、#11311、#11318、#11319、#11320 — 一条高度堆叠的链条（发布产物、快速开始安装、webhook 入口、RPC 分发）。每个 PR 都依赖更早的 PR，因此进展实际上被串行化。
  • 运行时能力边界 — #11174、#11187、#11526 — 接收能力参数的轮次构造器，并遵循传入的能力边界。
  • 提供商灵活性 — #9809（每个提供商配置可包含多个模型）与 #11659（snake_case 上下文溢出码）。

4. 社区热门话题

按更新项中的评论数排序：

条目 评论数 主题
#11254 RFC：A2A 协议 crate 7 横切架构 / 线路模型
#7432 运行时与网关交付追踪 6 版本规划
#10025 RFC：带 TUI 的临时智能体集群 4 多智能体编排
#11074 RFC：search_routes 提供商路由 4 工具/搜索路由
#11235 RFC：知识语料库（RAG） 4 记忆/检索

底层需求分析：

  • 互操作性占主导。#11254 构建在已确立的 A2A 工作（#9106、#7763、#8274）之上，表明用户希望 ZeroClaw 使用标准 agent-to-agent 协议，而不是定制协议。
  • 多智能体编排是第二个反复出现的主题——#10025（集群）、#11664（Dark Factory 工作流）和 #11667（命令策略继承）都指向用户已超出单智能体模型。
  • 检索增强式依据（#11235）反映出用户要求智能体能够基于运营方自有文档作答，而不只是依赖其参数化知识。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

按严重程度排序。较新的报告似乎尚未关联修复 PR。

S1 — 工作流受阻：

  • #11648 [Bug] — Web 仪表盘配对输入被限制为 6 位数字，但后端默认 PairingCodePolicy 现在签发 32 位字母数字字符。CLI 会打印完整配对码，但 Web 对话框会拒绝它，实际上阻止了 Web 端上手。用户影响高；很可能是一个快速前端修复。

S2 — 行为降级：

  • #11655 [Bug] — 在默认 embedding_provider = "none" 下，当不存在向量分数时，consolidate_turn / conflict::check_and_resolve_conflicts 会软隐藏无关的 Core 记忆。这是一个接近数据丢失的回归，影响默认配置，使其成为今日最令人担忧的稳定性问题。

S3 — 轻微：

  • #11658 [Bug] — Web 聊天输入框在回复后不会重新获得焦点，需要额外点击一次。严重性低，但在主界面中造成恼人的 UX 摩擦。

相关未决的正确性/架构问题：

  • #10290 — 将实时配置句柄贯穿 agent::run，用于分离的对等/子智能体轮次（SSRF 策略传播缺口）。
  • #7692（已接受）— 网关路由器请求体限制与 cron 运行超时接线测试仍然缺失；PR #10310 实现了这些测试，并且处于开启状态，等待作者处理。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

今日新增/更新的请求：

  • #11664 — Level 5 Dark Factory 工作流：具备生命周期管理的完全编排式智能体团队。
  • #11662 — 将 Channels 从 Core 中分离：模块化通道接口（IPC、MQTT 等），以便丢弃未使用的通道，因其是“累赘和安全风险”。
  • #11668 — 让网关 MAX_BODY_SIZE 可配置，并返回恰当的错误码 + 大小（由多智能体 A2A 中继长上下文问题驱动）。
  • #11657 — 轮次整合的可配置目标类别（[memory] consolidation_category）。
  • #11667 — 决定委派轮次是否继承调用方的命令策略。

下一版本预测（v0.8.6 / v0.9.0）：

  • 可配置网关请求体限制（#11668）是一个范围明确的小需求，且有具体用例（A2A 长上下文中继），是近期补丁的有力候选。
  • 通道模块化（#11662）直接契合 #7432 中 v0.9.0 的“网关分离”主题——有可能进入 v0.9.0。
  • 集群/Dark Factory 编排（#10025、#11664）很可能在 v0.9.0 之后，因为它依赖仍未合并的 A2A 与能力边界工作。
  • 多模型提供商配置（#9809，自 8 月 7 日起开启）与 RAG/知识语料库（#11235）是更大的押注，很可能面向 v1.0 跟踪。

7. 用户反馈摘要

痛点：

  • Web UI 中的上手流程已损坏。 配对码不匹配（#11648，S1）意味着用户按照文档流程操作时，会在浏览器中撞上硬墙。再加上焦点缺陷（#11658），Web 仪表盘正在产生最直接的负面反馈。
  • 默认设置导致静默数据丢失。 #11655 影响开箱即用配置（embedding_provider = "none"），因此从未自定义设置的用户会暴露在风险中。这削弱了对记忆子系统的信任。
  • 多智能体用户感到摩擦。 #11668 报告网关请求体限制会在“不到 1 秒内，仅以裸字符串 length limit exceeded”拒绝长上下文 A2A 消息——不透明的错误阻塞了合法工作流。
  • 臃肿与安全焦虑。 #11662 表达了用户明确希望摆脱未使用通道的愿望，这些通道被描述为“累赘”和“安全风险”，表明用户想要精简、可审计的部署。

满意度信号： 用户参与度很高——提交详细 RFC、引用具体 commit SHA 和 PR 编号，并构建多智能体拓扑。这种成熟度表明存在满意的重度用户群，但未解决 RFC 的堆积和缓慢的合并速度有让他们受挫的风险。

8. 积压观察

因存续时间、规模或停滞状态而需要维护者关注的条目：

  • #9809 — 自 2026-08-07 开启（66+ 天），size:XL，risk:high，标记为 needs-author-action。每个提供商支持多模型是一项频繁被请求的能力，却已停滞超过两个月。最高优先级积压项。
  • #7692 — 自 2026-06-15 开启（约 4 个月），status:accepted，risk:high。网关测试覆盖缺口；其实施 PR #10310 也处于开启状态，并被标记为 needs-author-action。
  • #9597 — 自 2026-07-31 开启，status:in-progress，follow-up，risk:high。持久/可归因的对等智能体轮次；是集群工作的基础，但已停滞。
  • #10290 — 自 2026-08-24 开启，follow-up，risk:high，仅 1 条评论。分离轮次的实时配置传播（SSRF 策略正确性）；与安全相关但讨论不足。
  • #11289 — 被标记为 do-not-merge，尽管是一个实质性的安全 PR（稳定的 RPC 拒绝原因标识符）；可能因维护者决策而受阻。
  • 堆叠插件 PR 链（#11261 → #11262 → #11347 等）——8+ 个相互依赖的 PR 全部开启。这里任何单个合并决策都可能解除 v0.8.6 插件托管发布的阻塞；维护者在这条链上的吞吐量是值得关注的关键瓶颈。

健康度说明： 该项目在架构上雄心勃勃，且活跃度很有吸引力，但合并与开启比例（2:43）、大量 needs-author-action / needs-maintainer-review 标签，以及多个已开启 1–2 个月的 XL PR，表明存在审查瓶颈。清理插件栈和长期停滞的 #9809 将实质性改善发布节奏和贡献者留存。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-12

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-12 08:27 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-12

1. Today’s Overview

OpenClaw remains highly active: 500 issues were updated in the last 24 hours (357 open/active, 143 closed), and 500 PRs were updated (363 open, 137 merged/closed), alongside two new releases. The latest releases focus almost entirely on update reliability, with v2026.10.2 fixing clean in-place upgrades from stable 2026.10.1 and v2026.10.5-beta.1 hardening updates across devices, filesystems, Windows elevation, and interrupted activations. However, the issue tracker shows persistent high-severity stability problems, especially memory leaks, zombie processes, update failures, session-state loss, and plugin-capture performance regressions. Project health is therefore mixed: maintenance throughput is high, but unresolved P0/P1 issues continue to affect production deployments, particularly on Windows, npm-global installs, and complex container/filesystem setups.

2. Releases

v2026.10.2

Link: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.2

Highlights from the release notes:

  • The first upgrade from stable 2026.10.1 now completes cleanly.
  • Successful in-place updates no longer end in errors.
  • Windows, cloned-filesystem, and private-Node update paths finish instead of stalling or rolling back.
  • Referenced fixes: #168849, #169031.

v2026.10.5-beta.1

Link: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.5-beta.1

Highlights from the release notes:

  • Safer updates across devices, filesystems, Windows elevation, and interrupted activations.
  • Recovery from stale leases or changed evidence instead of stranding the install or blocking future updates.
  • Referenced fixes: #164636, #164769, #165257, #165863, plus one truncated reference.

Breaking changes / migration notes: The provided release notes do not mention explicit breaking changes. The primary migration signal is improved resilience in update paths, which should reduce manual recovery for failed upgrades. That said, many open issues still report update failures across npm-global, Windows, LXC, and Windows multi-agent installs, so operators should still back up state before major upgrades.

3. Project Progress

  • PRs merged/closed today: 137.
  • Issues closed today: 143.

Closed issues indicate fixes landed in several areas:

  • Update reliability: #164113 — update failed at updater-runtime-retention with FICLONE EPERM inside unprivileged LXC; closed with a queueable fix. Link: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164113
  • Package recovery: #167506 — deleted temporary handoff database blocked package recovery and future updates; closed. Link: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/167506
  • Session state: #69118 — Claude CLI sessions reset on every turn in group channels due to groupIntro drift; closed as already fixed. Link: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/69118
  • Model request serialization: #123265 — role:"custom" runtime-context carrier was serialized as a trailing user message on every request; closed. Link: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123265
  • Memory/CPU saturation: #136175 — full local memory reindex saturated CPU and blocked diagnostics; closed. Link: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/136175
  • Sub-agent idempotency: #37446 — sub-agent timeout recovery created duplicate API posts; closed. Link: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/37446

A large share of open PR activity is driven by maintainer steipete, focused on architectural simplification and moving synchronous SQLite work off the Gateway thread:

  • #169648 — simplify state and process worker lifecycles. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169648
  • #169584 — prepare execution policy through workers. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169584
  • #169580 — move Gateway state consumers through existing workers. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169580
  • #169566 — route session forks, reads, and cleanup through workers. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169566
  • #169735 — avoid redundant reminder and session snapshot SQL. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169735
  • #169707 — reduce Control UI cold-load chat rendering. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169707
  • #169709 — reduce idle Gateway event-loop sampling work. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169709

There is also a significant open P1 PR aimed at safer updates:

  • #144005 — “back up state before migrations and restore it on rollback.” Still open, marked needs proof, large scope. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144005

4. Community Hot Topics

Most active issues by comment count:

  1. #91588 — P0 Gateway memory leak (38 comments)
    RSS grows from ~350 MB to 15.5 GB over days, causing repeated OOM crashes. No new fix PR.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91588

  2. #159356 — llama.cpp manager reports ready while embedding child exits (26 comments)
    Embedding requests return HTTP 500 “Failed to read connection”; P2 but impacts session state and crash loops.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159356

  3. #97616 — P1 unreaped hook/tool child processes (18 comments)
    Zombie accumulation under the main openclaw process causes runtime degradation.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97616

  4. #148707 — P1 reply lost with “no active tool authority snapshot” (18 comments)
    2026.9.4 regression: a second run displaces an in-flight turn and the reply is lost.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/148707

  5. #160959 — P0 Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins (15 comments)
    2026.9.6 regression; event loop blocked at startup and model runtime republish.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160959

  6. #86996 — Active Memory + Codex app-server path causes latency and stalls (15 comments, closed)
    Long response latency, hook timeouts, startup aborts, and Gateway event-loop stalls.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/86996

  7. #157989 — P1 plugin source capture rewrites ~1.1–1.4 GB per CLI command (15 comments)
    ~6.5 GB per Gateway start with no reuse; severe SSD wear.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/157989

Underlying needs: Users are consistently asking for resource stability, update reliability, plugin performance, and session/message durability. The highest-comment issues are not feature requests but production-impacting reliability gaps, many tagged clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr or needs-maintainer-review, suggesting maintainer attention is the bottleneck rather than lack of reports.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity from the provided data:

P0 / Critical

  • #91588 — Gateway memory leak, RSS 350 MB → 15.5 GB, repeated OOM crashes. Open, 38 comments, no new fix PR.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91588
  • #160959 — Gateway event loop blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression). Open, 15 comments, no new fix PR.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160959
  • #156112 — openclaw update fails at global install swap while direct npm install -g succeeds. Open, 14 comments, marked manual-only.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156112
  • #167652 — Windows Gateway hangs after 2026.9.9 upgrade despite Doctor reporting verified restart. Open, 8 comments, P0, release blocker.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/167652
  • #126821 — SQLite corruption recurs on pristine rebuilt DBs within 15–24h (WSL2), including paralyzed gateway mode. Open, 9 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/126821
  • #112475 — Device pairing recovery fails after removal. Open, 8 comments, P0.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/112475
  • #155191 — Native memory leak in 2026.9.5: RSS grows ~1 GiB per 30s while V8 heap stays stable. Open, 8 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/155191

P1 / High

  • #97616 — Leaked/unreaped hook and tool child processes cause zombie accumulation and runtime degradation. Open, 18 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97616
  • #148707 — Reply lost with “Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot” on displaced in-flight turn. Open, 18 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/148707
  • #145309 — claude-cli backend ignores CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, causing missing-transcript resets and failover. Open, 12 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/145309
  • #104719 — memory-wiki supplement exhaustive fallback ignores tool deadline. Open, 12 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/104719
  • #168955 — Startup regression in 2026.10.1 on Windows: ready ~1030s vs ~410s on 2026.9.9. Open, 10 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/168955
  • #158788 — Cron agent turns fail at setup with DataCloneError on Windows (2026.9.6). Open, 8 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/158788
  • #159512 — claude-cli: every subagent completion invalidates requester CLI session twice. Open, 7 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159512
  • #107244 — WhatsApp group messages never reach inbound handling; DMs work. Open, 7 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107244
  • #126950 — Telegram opaque callback payloads (tgcb1:) silently dropped for non-plugin callers. Open, 7 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/126950
  • #54488 — Session lane starvation: followup drain monopolizes lane, blocks inbound dispatch for 20–30min. Open, 7 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/54488

P2 / Moderate

  • #159356 — llama.cpp manager reports ready while embedding child exits; embedding requests return HTTP 500. Open, 26 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159356
  • #105528 — exec/read tools silently return empty output on Windows (2026.6.x regression). Open, 10 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/105528
  • #120385 — Code Mode tool catalog incomplete for scheduled/cron and memory-flush turns; MCP tools missing. Open, 10 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/120385
  • #164394 — Control UI WebChat transcript jitters continuously when scrolling into history. Open, 9 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164394
  • #162914 — Intermittent “Aborted | sandbox_provisioning” failures with rootless Podman sandbox. Open, 9 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162914
  • #48709 — Gemini 2.5 Pro: textSignature bloat, think tags, mixed text/tool causing session failures. Open, 8 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48709
  • #99659 — OpenClaw OOM-killed after companion app connected. Open, 7 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99659
  • #166894 — Gateway restart sometimes hangs 30+ minutes to 2 hours on Windows multi-agent installs (2026.9.8). Open, 7 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166894
  • #124759 — iOS app lags badly when “show reasoning and tool activity” is enabled. Open, 7 comments.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/124759

Fix PR status: Many high-severity issues carry clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr, meaning no linked fix PR is visible in the provided data. Some closed issues — #164113, #167506, #69118, #123265, #136175, #37446 — indicate fixes have recently landed for update recovery, session hashing, request serialization, and sub-agent idempotency.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #50093 — WhatsApp: backfill missed messages after reconnection. P1, open, 14 comments. Users lose messages during outage windows.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50093

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent OSS Ecosystem

Window: 2026-10-11 → 2026-10-12 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

Method note: Activity figures are taken directly from each project's 24-hour digest. Health scores are analyst-assigned composites (1–10) weighing activity throughput, closure ratio, release cadence, critical-backlog severity, and community engagement — they are not vendor- or GitHub-provided metrics. OpenClaw's issue/PR counts appear capped at the 500-item API ceiling and should be read as "≥500."

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent OSS landscape is functionally converging while structurally diverging. Nearly every active project is independently rebuilding the same core stack — a gateway, a plugin/extension runtime, MCP tool plumbing, a memory/compaction layer, multi-channel ingress, and provider-agnostic model routing — but with sharply different language, packaging, and target-user bets. The dominant unsolved problem across all five projects is not capability but operational reliability: install/update fragility, gateway resource leaks, session durability, and plugin sandboxing cost appear in every backlog, and the highest-engagement community threads are production-incident reports rather than feature requests. A second cross-cutting constraint is maintainer review bandwidth: contributor supply is healthy in QwenPaw and ZeroClaw, yet merge latency — not idea scarcity — is the binding constraint.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tier 1 — Hyper-scale, capacity-constrained: OpenClaw. Highest velocity in the ecosystem, but operating in reactive mode against a P0 backlog. Fastest releases (2 in 24h), but releases have been narrowly update-focused while memory/process leaks persist for months.

Tier 2 — Actively stabilizing and shipping: Hermes Agent. The most balanced profile: high throughput, a release actually shipped, meaningful security and lifecycle issues closed (#25793, #105239, #127450), and a coherent in-flight fix wave (compression retry, Windows status probe, TUI locking). Best current health-to-scale ratio.

Tier 3 — Improving but release-starved: QwenPaw. Strong contribution flow (57% PR closure), aggressive backlog cleanup of 6-month-old PRs, and high-quality community reports — but no release while v2.2.x regressions accumulate (#8173, #8179, #8175). The single highest-leverage action is cutting a release.

Tier 3b — Design-heavy, review-bottlenecked: ZeroClaw. Six simultaneous high-risk RFCs, architecturally ambitious, deeply engaged power users — but a 4.4% PR closure rate and a 50-day-stale wasm-adjacent PR (#7834-adjacent chain). Iterating on design more than on code.

Tier 4 — Quiet maintenance: IronClaw. Zero issues, zero human contributions, dependabot-only activity. Either a mature/frozen codebase or a dormancy signal — undeterminable from this snapshot.

Iterating rapidly: OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw. Stabilizing: Hermes, QwenPaw. Designing: ZeroClaw. Quiescent: IronClaw.

7. Trend Signals

1. Reliability is the product, not a feature. Across all five projects, the highest-comment items are incident reports: memory leaks, FD exhaustion, zombie processes, silent data corruption. For developers: resource hygiene (RSS, FDs, child processes), atomic state, and crash recovery are now table stakes for adoption — not roadmap items.

2. Updates/installs are becoming a first-class subsystem. Cross-platform elevation semantics, rollback-on-failure, and backup-before-migration appear independently in OpenClaw (PR #144005), Hermes (#126860), and QwenPaw (#8179). For developers: design the update path with atomicity and privilege-boundary awareness from day one; it is a top-three source of user churn.

3. Plugin sandboxing is shifting to WASM and process isolation. IronClaw (wasmtime), ZeroClaw (WASM hosting chain), and QwenPaw (#8187 subprocess isolation) are all moving away from in-process plugin execution. OpenClaw's GB-per-command source capture is a cautionary counter-example. For developers: choose an isolation boundary before the plugin API stabilizes — retrofitting is expensive.

4. Memory/context management is the new frontier of correctness. Compaction, context overflow recovery, token budgets, and RAG corpora appear in all five. Critically, the failure mode users complain about is silent and destructive — QwenPaw's binary corruption (#8179), ZeroClaw's default-config memory hiding (#11655), Hermes's opaque /memory approve all (#136738).

5. Silent failures are the single most-cited dissatisfaction pattern. QwenPaw (#8173, #8175, #8179), OpenClaw (#159356 embedding child exits while "ready"), and Hermes (#135522 silently denied approval) all surface identical language: "no log, no error." For developers: debuggability and explicit failure surfaces are a competitive feature, especially for self-hosted operators.

6. Protocol interoperability is consolidating around MCP and A2A. MCP is now assumed in OpenClaw, Hermes, and QwenPaw; A2A is ZeroClaw's strategic bet (#11254). For developers: build tool and agent interfaces against these protocols rather than bespoke wire formats — expected lifetime is longer.

7. Multi-agent orchestration is moving from experiment to product. Kanban workers (Hermes), sub-agent idempotency (OpenClaw), worker containers (QwenPaw), and swarms/Dark Factory (ZeroClaw) indicate users are outgrowing single-agent topologies and need lifecycle, isolation, and policy-inheritance primitives.

8. Provider quirks remain an unabstracted tax. DeepSeek, Z.AI, Gemini, claude-cli, Codex, and custom-prefix providers each generate project-specific bugs. For developers: assume provider heterogeneity is permanent; treat model routing, token-limit defaults, and credential paths as configurable surfaces, not constants.

9. Review bandwidth, not contributor supply, is the ecosystem's binding constraint. OpenClaw (maintainer-tagged needs-maintainer-review), QwenPaw (~6-month PR latency, now clearing), and ZeroClaw (2:43 merge ratio) all exhibit the same pathology.

10. Cost and hardware externality are becoming UX concerns. OpenClaw's ~6.5 GB/start plugin capture causing SSD wear (#157989) is an early signal that resource efficiency is entering the user-facing value proposition for long-running agent deployments.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-10-12

Source: github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw showed high maintenance throughput on 2026-10-12: 13 issues and 23 PRs were touched in the last 24 hours, with 13 PRs merged/closed against 10 still open. Notably, a large fraction of today's closures are long-stalled PRs from March–July 2026 (MCP hardening, context-overflow recovery, plugin-market version routing, memory backend), indicating an active backlog-cleanup push rather than purely new work. Issue traffic remains dominated by stability regressions in v2.2.x Desktop and Codex-backend paths, plus a growing cluster of Console/UX polish requests. No new release shipped, so users on v2.2.1/2.2.2-beta are running fixes only from unreleased branches. Overall health is good on contribution flow, strained on release cadence — the volume of open, unfixed v2.2.x bug reports is accumulating faster than releases can absorb them.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24 hours. Latest observable user-reported versions in the wild are v2.2.1 (stable), v2.2.2-beta.4, and v2.1.1b2 (older Desktop build). The absence of a release is notable given the number of merged fixes queued (see §3).

3. Project Progress — Merged / Closed PRs

13 PRs were merged or closed. The clear themes:

Plugin ecosystem correctness

  • #5661 — Filter plugin market and CDN catalog by QwenPaw version compatibility (qwenpaw_version / min_version / max_version).
  • #5612 — Plugin market download routes isolated by major version (v1.x vs v2.x incompatibility fix).

Runtime resilience

  • #2783 — Auto-recover context-window overflow via one-shot memory compaction + retry.
  • #2520 — Preflight active-model availability; reject activation with explicit errors.
  • #1977 — Harden MCP teardown, cron/channel exception handling.
  • #2052 — Degrade MCP connection errors to tool-level failures instead of chat-visible errors.

MCP + tooling

  • #1978 — MCP import validation/preview + runtime status diagnostics.
  • #4707 — Robust ToolResponse text-block handling (attribute vs dict access crash).

Configurability

  • #5732 — New none memory backend to fully disable the memory system via Console.

Desktop UX

  • #5569 — Two-phase splash loading to eliminate the 5–30s Windows startup white screen.

Three additional PRs closed without detail in the supplied dataset.

Assessment: the closures are mostly foundational hardening rather than headline features. Several directly address pain points still being reported by users today (context overflow, MCP noise, plugin incompatibility), which suggests the fixes may resolve open issues once a release ships.

4. Community Hot Topics

Rank Item Comments Signal
1 #7311 — v2.1.1b2 missing _qwenpaw_remote_backend, all tools broken 5 Closed today. Highest-engagement item; total tool failure on Windows Desktop.
2 #7016 — Streaming tool-call 404 / Tool call not found 4 Still open since 2026-08-14 — ~2 months unresolved.
3 #8174 — Tavily provider has no API-key config surface 3 Paid-quota users blocked; active discussion.

Underlying needs analysis:

  • #7311 / #7016 both point at fragile remote-backend and tool-call lifecycle plumbing. The 404 loop in #7016 (offload endpoint repeatedly 404ing during streaming) suggests a session/tool-call registry desynchronization under streaming — the same class of failure that produces "all tools broken" symptoms. This is the single most impactful reliability area in the project right now.
  • #8174 reflects a monetization/self-hosting expectation mismatch: QwenPaw ships a built-in provider that silently uses keyless anonymous mode, with no UI to inject a user key. Users with paid API access are effectively blocked — a common pattern when built-in integrations hard-code a credential path.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

Critical

  • #7311 — [CLOSED] All agent tools fail (ModuleNotFoundError: _qwenpaw_remote_backend) on v2.1.1b2 Windows Desktop; module absent from _internal. Closed today — no fix PR explicitly linked in the dataset, so resolution should be verified before users assume a fix shipped.

High

  • #8173 — Codex backend silently loses harness↔codex connection after restart; leaves a permanent zombie running entry that blocks all recovery paths (only chat/stop works). Affects v2.2.1. No fix PR identified.
  • #7016 — Streaming tool-call offload returns 404 in a loop; tool-call not found. Open ~59 days. No fix PR identified.
  • #8179 — qwenpaw skills install <github-url> silently corrupts all binary files (non-UTF-8 → U+FFFD), breaking images/fonts in installed skills. Data-integrity class bug, v2.2.1 Docker.
  • #8175 — ProviderManager.active_model not loaded at startup, combined with silent except Exception: pass in _load_agent_model_settings; causes nightly cron (dream) failures across multi-agent deployments.

Medium

  • #8184 — Doom-loop gate kills legitimate task-authorized polling; cron then records false success after termination. False-positive guard logic.
  • #8185 — desktop.log never rotates on Windows; sidecar tee handle defeats _SafeRotatingFileHandler. Disk-growth risk.
  • #8186 — Console message-navigation jump overrides manual wheel scrolling, snapping back to anchor for ~1.6s.
  • #8176 — Plugin Store "Update All" skips third-party plugins (v2.2.1).

Low / Config

  • #8177 — Hardcoded /console basename blocks reverse-proxy subpath deployments.

Fix PRs in flight:

  • #8188 — Fixes approval decision race (references #8105): decision lost → tool rejected despite prior approval.
  • #8183 — Preserves cancellation reasons; returns ERROR for recoverable timeouts so the parent agent loop continues.
  • #8182 — Server-side persistence of per-chat approval level (directly relevant to #8180).
  • #7973 — Recover from rejected media URLs (HTTP 400 on media → perpetual conversation failure).

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Issue / PR Request Likelihood for next release
#8174 Tavily API-key config surface Medium-High — small UI/config change, high user impact
#8181 Session-level change notifications (long-lived event channel) to avoid hard refresh Medium — architectural, touches SSE/streaming layer
#8180 + #8182 Session-scoped approval level persisted server-side High — PR already open, closes a documented UX/semantics gap
#8177 Configurable console basename for reverse proxies Medium — common self-host ask, low complexity
#8176 "Update All" should include third-party plugins Medium-High — pairs with today's plugin-market PR closures
#8178 Nested/categorised skill directories Medium — PR open, backward-compatible
#8187 Extract channels into plugins with subprocess isolation Low for next minor (XXXL, architectural)
#8164 Native HarmonyOS client (ArkUI/ArkTS) Low for next minor (XXXL, new platform)
#8137 Official "reduced effects" accessibility tier Medium-High — small, self-contained
#8156 Coding-CLI management endpoints for worker containers Medium — multi-agent deployment need

Prediction: The next release is most likely dominated by Console/server-state consistency (#8182, #8137, #8177) and plugin-market correctness (#8176, building on today's #5661/#5612 closures), with stability fixes from #8188/#8183/#7973 folded in.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  • Tool reliability is the #1 complaint — #7311 (all tools broken), #7016 (404 loops), #8184 (doom-loop false positives), #8188-related approval races. Users are hitting failures at the tool-execution layer, which is core to an agent product.
  • Silent failures are a recurring motif: #8175 (silent except Exception: pass), #8179 (silent binary corruption), #8173 (silent connection break leaving zombie state). Users explicitly call out "no log, no error" behavior.
  • Self-hosting friction: #8177 (reverse-proxy subpath) and #8179 (Docker install) show the self-hosted segment is a real, vocal constituency with unmet deployment needs.
  • Credential/config opacity: #8174 — users cannot tell that built-in Tavily uses keyless mode, nor supply their own key.

Satisfaction signals:

  • High-quality, well-structured bug reports (structured templates, version pins, environment details) indicate an engaged, technically capable community willing to invest effort in the project.
  • Several first-time and repeat contributors are active (#8178 first-time, #6499 first-time), which is a positive health signal.

Use cases revealed: multi-agent Docker deployments with per-workspace configs (#8175), cron/dream overnight jobs, multi-channel sessions needing cross-device consistency (#8181), and worker containers running third-party coding CLIs (#8156).

8. Backlog Watch — Needs Maintainer Attention

Item Age Why it matters
#7016 — Streaming tool-call 404 59 days open High-severity, repeatedly reproduced, no linked fix. Longest-lived unresolved core bug.
#7973 — Recover from rejected media URLs 18 days open Fix ready but unmerged; conversation-breaking bug persists in the meantime.
#6499 — Add Atlas Cloud provider ~77 days open First-time-contributor PR, self-contained, blocks contributor momentum if left idle.
#8183 — Preserve cancellation reasons 0 days (new) Directly relevant to #8184-class false-positive terminations; worth fast-tracking together.
#8156 — Coding-CLI management endpoints 3 days Multi-agent ops gap; no maintainer response evident.
#1977, #2783, #2520 ~200 days each (now closed) Welcome resolution, but the ~6-month latency on meaningful robustness PRs is a review-throughput red flag worth addressing structurally.

Backlog health verdict: The project is clearly processing its backlog today, but the multi-month lag on #1977/#2783/#2520/#4707 shows the bottleneck is maintainer review capacity, not contributor supply. Combined with no release in 24h and a cluster of open v2.2.x regressions, the highest-leverage action would be to cut a release that ships the just-merged fixes.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-12

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw showed high-velocity, low-throughput engineering activity on 2026-10-12: 45 PRs and 16 issues were touched in the last 24 hours, but only 2 PRs closed and 0 issues closed, with no new releases. The project is deep in a design-heavy phase, with six high-risk RFCs open simultaneously covering an A2A protocol crate, ephemeral agent swarms, RAG/knowledge corpus, provider routing, and runtime/gateway separation — most awaiting maintainer review or author action. A large, stacked body of PR work from a small set of contributors (IftekharUddin, JordanTheJet, NiuBlibing) is driving plugin/WASM hosting, capability-boundary refactors, and gateway hardening, but nearly all of it sits open and unmerged. Meanwhile, a steady drip of user-facing bug reports (pairing codes, web chat focus, memory consolidation) indicates real-world onboarding friction that is being filed faster than it is being resolved. Overall health: strong contributor engagement and clear roadmap direction, but a widening merge backlog and a notable gap between accepted trackers/RFCs and shipped code.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24 hours. Several open PRs carry release:v0.8.6 and release:v0.9.0 labels, indicating both lines are still in-flight:

  • #7432 — Tracker for Phase 2 runtime work (v0.8.6) and Phase 3 gateway separation (v0.9.0)
  • #11187, #11261, #11262, #11347 — all tagged for v0.8.6

No breaking changes or migration notes to report today.

3. Project Progress

Only 2 PRs were merged/closed in the 24-hour window, versus 43 still open — a notably lopsided ratio.

Closed today:

  • #11531 [CLOSED] — fix(tunnel): report the URL tailscale actually serves the gateway on. Fixed a real misreporting bug where the gateway advertised https://<host>:<local_port> while Tailscale actually served HTTPS on port 443. Small (size:XS), from a distinguished contributor.

Advancing but not yet merged (high-signal clusters):

  • Plugin/WASM infrastructure stack — #11261, #11262, #11347, #11309, #11311, #11318, #11319, #11320 — a deeply stacked chain (release artifacts, quickstart install, webhook ingress, RPC dispatch). Each depends on earlier PRs, so progress is effectively serialized.
  • Runtime capability boundaries — #11174, #11187, #11526 — capability-taking turn constructors and honoring supplied capability boundaries.
  • Provider flexibility — #9809 (multiple models per provider profile) and #11659 (snake_case context-overflow codes).

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count among updated items:

Item Comments Theme
#11254 RFC: A2A protocol crate 7 Cross-cutting architecture / wire model
#7432 Runtime & gateway delivery tracker 6 Release planning
#10025 RFC: ephemeral agent swarms w/ TUI 4 Multi-agent orchestration
#11074 RFC: search_routes provider routing 4 Tool/search routing
#11235 RFC: Knowledge corpus (RAG) 4 Memory/retrieval

Underlying needs analysis:

  • Interoperability dominates. #11254 builds on established A2A work (#9106, #7763, #8274) and signals users want ZeroClaw to speak a standard agent-to-agent protocol rather than a bespoke one.
  • Orchestration of multiple agents is the second recurring theme — #10025 (swarms), #11664 (Dark Factory workflow), and #11667 (command-policy inheritance) all point to users outgrowing the single-agent model.
  • Retrieval-augmented grounding (#11235) reflects demand for the agent to answer from operator-owned documents rather than only its parametric knowledge.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity. No fix PRs appear linked to the newer reports yet.

S1 — Workflow blocked:

  • #11648 [Bug] — Web dashboard pairing input is limited to 6 digits, but the backend default PairingCodePolicy now issues 32 alphanumeric characters. The CLI prints the full code, but the web dialog rejects it, effectively blocking web onboarding. High user impact; likely a quick frontend fix.

S2 — Degraded behavior:

  • #11655 [Bug] — With the default embedding_provider = "none", consolidate_turn / conflict::check_and_resolve_conflicts soft-hides unrelated Core memories when no vector scores exist. This is a data-loss-adjacent regression affecting the default configuration, making it the most concerning stability issue today.

S3 — Minor:

  • #11658 [Bug] — Web chat input does not regain focus after a reply, requiring an extra click. Low severity but annoying UX friction in the primary interface.

Related open correctness/architecture issues:

  • #10290 — Thread live config handle through agent::run for detached peer/subagent turns (SSRF policy propagation gap).
  • #7692 (accepted) — Gateway router body-limit and cron-run timeout wiring tests still missing; PR #10310 implements these tests and is open, awaiting author action.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

New/updated requests today:

  • #11664 — Level 5 Dark Factory Workflow: fully orchestrated agent teams with lifecycle management.
  • #11662 — Separate Channels from Core: modular channel interface (IPC, MQTT, etc.) to drop unused channels as "deadweight and security risk."
  • #11668 — Make gateway MAX_BODY_SIZE configurable and return a proper error code + size (driven by multi-agent A2A relay of long-context questions).
  • #11657 — Configurable target category for turn consolidation ([memory] consolidation_category).
  • #11667 — Decide whether delegated turns inherit the caller's command policy.

Prediction for next version (v0.8.6 / v0.9.0):

  • Configurable gateway body limits (#11668) is a small, well-scoped ask with a concrete use case (A2A long-context relay) and is a strong candidate for a near-term patch.
  • Channel modularization (#11662) aligns directly with the v0.9.0 "gateway separation" theme in #7432 — plausible for v0.9.0.
  • Swarm/Dark Factory orchestration (#10025, #11664) is likely post-v0.9.0, as it depends on the still-unmerged A2A and capability-boundary work.
  • Multi-model provider profiles (#9809, open since Aug 7) and RAG/knowledge corpus (#11235) are larger bets likely tracked for v1.0.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Onboarding is broken in the web UI. The pairing-code mismatch (#11648, S1) means a user following documented flows hits a hard wall in the browser. Combined with the focus bug (#11658), the web dashboard is generating the most immediate negative feedback.
  • Default settings cause silent data loss. #11655 affects the out-of-the-box configuration (embedding_provider = "none"), so users who never customize settings are exposed. This undermines trust in the memory subsystem.
  • Multi-agent users feel friction. #11668 reports gateway body limits rejecting long-context A2A messages "in < 1 s with the bare string length limit exceeded" — opaque errors blocking legitimate workflows.
  • Bloat and security anxiety. #11662 voices a clear user desire to shed unused channels described as "deadweight" and a "security risk," suggesting users want lean, auditable deployments.

Satisfaction signals: Users are deeply engaged — filing detailed RFCs, referencing specific commit SHAs and PR numbers, and building multi-agent topologies. This level of sophistication suggests a satisfied power-user base, but the accumulation of unresolved RFCs and the slow merge rate risk frustrating them.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention due to age, size, or stalled status:

  • #9809 — Open since 2026-08-07 (66+ days), size:XL, risk:high, tagged needs-author-action. Multi-model-per-provider is a frequently requested capability stuck for over two months. Highest-priority backlog item.
  • #7692 — Open since 2026-06-15 (~4 months), status:accepted, risk:high. Gateway test coverage gap; its implementing PR #10310 is also open and flagged needs-author-action.
  • #9597 — Open since 2026-07-31, status:in-progress, follow-up, risk:high. Durable/attributable peer-agent turns; foundational for the swarm work but stalled.
  • #10290 — Open since 2026-08-24, follow-up, risk:high, only 1 comment. Live-config propagation for detached turns (SSRF policy correctness); security-relevant and under-discussed.
  • #11289 — Marked do-not-merge despite being a substantial security PR (stable RPC denial reason identifiers); likely blocked on a maintainer decision.
  • Stacked plugin PR chain (#11261 → #11262 → #11347 etc.) — 8+ interdependent PRs all open. Any single merge decision here could unblock the v0.8.6 plugin hosting release; maintainer throughput on this chain is the key bottleneck to watch.

Health note: The project is architecturally ambitious and attractively active, but the merge-to-open ratio (2:43), the volume of needs-author-action / needs-maintainer-review labels, and multiple XL PRs open for 1–2 months indicate a review bottleneck. Clearing the plugin stack and the long-stalled #9809 would materially improve both release cadence and contributor retention.

横向对比

跨项目 AI 基础设施报告 — 2026-10-12

1. 生态系统概览

AI 基础设施生态系统正处于加固阶段，而非以发布为主的阶段：六个项目中有四个没有发布新版本，关注点主要集中在正确性回归、硬件适配以及面向智能体的协议缺口上。数据中心服务引擎正在 MoE、MLA/注意力 kernel、量化 KV cache 和非 NVIDIA 后端上展开竞争，同时还要应对前缀缓存和投机解码中的静默损坏问题。本地运行时正在扩展后端覆盖和工具调用，但多租户缓存隔离以及 Apple MLX/CUDA/Vulkan 稳定性仍是薄弱环节。网关和训练栈正在向更高层演进：LiteLLM 聚焦于 MCP 鉴权、协议转换和费用准确性；Unsloth 则关注静默训练失败、KV 抢占以及让 Studio 可由智能体驱动。在各层中，主导型工作负载形态是 MoE、量化、长上下文/前缀复用以及使用工具的智能体。

4. 性能前沿

优化集中在七个领域：

  • KV cache 与前缀复用： vLLM 在混合/状态空间和投机路径上存在严重的前缀缓存损坏；SGLang 报告 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 多轮前缀缓存退化为恒定的约 11.5K token 命中；llama.cpp 在并发下存在 prompt 缓存污染；Unsloth 正在为并行聊天添加 KV 抢占。
  • 投机解码： vLLM 的 DFlash2/DSpark + 前缀缓存会损坏输出；SGLang 的 DFLASH/DSPARK 存在重复、OOM 以及首个非贪婪请求崩溃；llama.cpp 在量化目标上出现贪婪输出分歧。
  • MoE 与路由： vLLM 扩展融合共享专家和 AITER 调优的 MoE 路由门控；SGLang 通过 aiter topk_gating 优化 512 专家 softmax MoE；llama.cpp 修复 Vulkan/Metal 上的重复专家 ID；Unsloth 标记 MoE-LoRA checkpoint 布局风险。
  • Attention/MLA 与量化 KV： vLLM 通过 FlashAttn MLA 路由 XPU MLA，并添加 ROCm FP8 MLA prefill；SGLang 致力于 QSA 上下文并行和 fp8 KV cache；llama.cpp 改进 OpenCL flash attention。
  • 分布式服务与批处理： vLLM 添加 DeepSeek-V4 ROCm 双批重叠，并为自适应 prefill token 预算提出 RFC；SGLang 推进 prefill 上下文并行、PD 分离和 Mooncake decode；llama.cpp 的 RPC 后端在大型 MoE 分片时崩溃。
  • 量化： vLLM 重度依赖 FP8/NVFP4，并有一个未解决的 INT8 KV 请求；SGLang 出现 fp8 KV + QSA 崩溃；llama.cpp 优化 CM2、Q4/Q8 和 SYCL Q4_0；Unsloth 聚焦 QLoRA/MLX 重打包。
  • Kernel 与后端： vLLM 使用 AITER、FlashInfer、Triton；SGLang 使用 FlashInfer autotune、aiter、Triton；llama.cpp 推进 Vulkan/OpenCL/SYCL/Hexagon；Ollama 与 MLX/CUDA/Vulkan 问题作斗争；Unsloth 移除 bitsandbytes 同步停顿。

前沿要点： 最快的收益不再只是“更多 FLOPS”。它们来自 paged/前缀缓存正确性、MoE 路由、量化注意力和后端专用 kernel — 而这些领域的回归可能会静默破坏输出质量。

5. 层次定位

层次 项目 角色 当前重点
服务引擎 vLLM、SGLang 高吞吐 GPU 服务器；paged attention、连续批处理、投机解码、分布式服务、多硬件 vLLM：ROCm/XPU/CUDA、MLA、MoE、前缀缓存正确性。SGLang：PD 分离、上下文并行、FlashInfer autotune、扩散/ComfyUI。
本地运行时 llama.cpp、Ollama 在本地/边缘运行模型；GGUF/GGML、广泛后端、简单 UX llama.cpp：ABI 可见性、Vulkan/OpenCL/SYCL/Metal 正确性、spec-decode 可靠性。Ollama：工具调用、MLX/CUDA/Vulkan 稳定性、打包。
网关/路由器 LiteLLM Provider 抽象、鉴权、费用跟踪、路由/故障转移、护栏、MCP MCP OAuth/工具目录、Anthropic↔OpenAI 转换、Gemini 计费、虚拟模型。
训练/微调 Unsloth 高效 LoRA/QLoRA、本地 Studio、微调 + 推理工作流 静默梯度 bug、MoE-LoRA 导出、KV 抢占、优化器同步移除、MCP 驱动 Studio。

重叠： vLLM 和 SGLang 可作为后端位于 LiteLLM 之后。Ollama 捆绑 llama.cpp 并增加 registry/API UX。Unsloth 可以训练模型并通过 Studio 本地提供服务，与本地运行时重叠。

6. 趋势信号

  1. 正确性成为新的性能瓶颈。 前缀缓存和投机解码在混合、状态空间和 MoE 模型上并非安全的默认选项。关注 vLLM #60174/#53912、SGLang #40843/#41076/#43412 以及 llama.cpp #25618/#27148。
  2. 硬件碎片化正在加速。 ROCm MI355X/gfx942、Intel XPU、SM120/Blackwell、Apple MLX、NPU、Vulkan/OpenCL/SYCL/Hexagon — 部署矩阵现在会实质性影响正确性和吞吐量。
  3. MoE 是默认的高端工作负载。 路由、重复专家 ID、融合专家、MoE LoRA 和量化 MoE 出现在 vLLM、SGLang、llama.cpp 和 Unsloth 中。
  4. 量化正在进入 KV cache 和注意力。 FP8、FP4/NVFP4、INT8 请求以及后端特定的 KV 行为现在是一级部署决策。
  5. 智能体工具链对生产至关重要，但仍然脆弱。 关注 Ollama 的 Qwen 3.8 流式 500 错误和 format: "json" 工具调用失败、vLLM 的 MiniMax-M3 流式工具调用边界情况，以及 LiteLLM 的 MCP OAuth/工具目录风险。
  6. 网关准确性与网关正常运行时间同样重要。 LiteLLM 的 Gemini 工具使用计费缺口、no-log 费用跳过以及 Anthropic↔OpenAI 转换缺口可能会扭曲租户预算或破坏 Claude Code 风格的客户端。
  7. 本地多租户服务需要默认隔离。 llama.cpp 由 RAM 支持的 prompt 缓存可能在并发下污染对话；Ollama 的 keep_alive 溢出和 Windows CUDA 损坏是运维陷阱。
  8. 微调仍然存在静默失败模式。 Unsloth 的 Gemma 4 融合损失零梯度 bug 和 MoE-LoRA checkpoint 布局隐患意味着团队必须验证梯度和导出，而不仅仅是损失曲线。

智能体/应用开发者现在应关注：

  • 如果使用前缀缓存、投机解码或混合/MoE 模型，请固定服务引擎版本。
  • 在流式和非流式模式下测试工具调用；在 Ollama 上，在 #18944 修复之前，避免将 format: "json" 与工具调用一起使用。
  • 将 MCP OAuth 刷新和工具目录固定视为 LiteLLM 中的生产问题。
  • 不要根据 Ollama 上兼容 OpenAI 的 timings.prompt_per_second 来基准化 LiteLLM 容量 — 它目前虚高。
  • 在发布 MoE 或 Gemma 4 适配器之前，验证微调梯度和 checkpoint 转换器。
  • 对于本地部署，在启用多租户并发之前，审计 prompt 缓存隔离和后端稳定性。

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM 摘要 — 2026-10-12

来源：github.com/vllm-project/vllm · 过去 24 小时更新 86 个 issue 和 464 个 PR · 无新版本发布

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时没有新版本发布，因此关注点仍集中在正确性和平台适配。最主要的主题是 混合/状态空间模型与投机解码路径上的前缀缓存损坏：多个独立报告（#60174、#53912、#57267、#57032）描述了缓存命中后的静默输出损坏，针对 GDN/MTP 情况的修复 PR 正在推进（#52244）。与此同时，ROCm 势头强劲：MI355X 上针对 Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B 和 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 的新性能追踪器，以及 Kimi-K3 mono-decode 正在从 gfx950 移植到 gfx942（#60997）。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

无。过去 24 小时没有发布新 tag 或 release artifact，今天也没有公布 API/配置格式变更。

给跟踪版本的人的提示：#60174 报告了一个 0.30.0 引入的行为回归（DFlash2/DSpark drafter 上的前缀缓存），因此对于该配置，0.29.x 是最后一个已知良好的版本线。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • Intel XPU — MLA 支持：PR #58297 通过现有的 FLASH_ATTN_MLA 后端在 XPU 上路由 MLA，使用 vllm-xpu-kernels 的 varlen flash attention，将 q = [q_nope, q_pe] 打包以对 latent cache 进行计算。
  • ROCm — MLA FP8 prefill（可选启用）：PR #59124 添加了 ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8，这是一个面向 MI355X（gfx950）上 Kimi-K3 的 FlyDSL FP8 MLA prefill 后端。
  • ROCm — gfx942 上的 Kimi-K3：PR #60997 将仅支持 gfx950 的 mono decode kernel 移植到 gfx942（256 个 CTA × 512 个线程，arch 现在成为 build key 的一部分）。
  • FlashInfer 0.7.1 升级：PR #60948 将 CUDA 和 Rubin 构建中的 flashinfer-python 从 0.7.0.post1 升级到 0.7.1，显式选择 CuTe DSL KDA prefill 后端，以避免 B200 Kimi-K3 CI 中出现的 inference-tensor 崩溃。
  • Embedding LoRA：PR #61033 为 BertModel、RobertaModel 和 XLMRobertaModel（BGE、all-MiniLM、multilingual-e5 系列）启用了 LoRA adapter。
  • 功能请求（开放中）：INT8 KV-cache 量化仍仅支持 FP8；请求跟踪于 #33480（22 条评论，12 👍）。

4. 性能与优化

已合入 / 评审中的 PR

  • DeepSeek-V4 ROCm：针对采用 flattened expert TP 的数据并行部署，prefill 计算/通信双批重叠（DBO）— #57773。
  • ROCm：通过 clean_logits=False 跳过 sparse prefill MQA-logits buffer 上的 torch.full(..., -inf) FP32 填充 — #51314。
  • ROCm：MoE router gate 使用 AITER 调优的 GEMM（此前受 Hopper/Blackwell 限制）— #50535。
  • ROCm：为 Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 启用融合 QK-norm + RoPE + gate 的 Triton kernel — #51406。
  • ROCm：GLM-5.3-Flash 的 AITER 融合 shared experts 扩展到 gfx942（MI300X/MI325X）上的 TP2/4/8 — #60604。

已报告的回归 / 尚未解决的性能差距

  • SM120 + DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash（8× RTX PRO 6000）：在 --enforce-eager 下 decode 吞吐极低，且 CUDA graphs 不可用；维护者被要求优先处理 SM120 graph capture — #56892。
  • SM120 上的 NVFP4 KV cache：causal paged prefill 实测约 145.8 ms，相比 FP8 慢约 1.7–1.8× — #50416。
  • RDNA4（gfx1201）：自 v0.28 起会选中 RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel，导致 decode 损失 5–24% — #57838。
  • Pooling 吞吐：自 torch 2.11 起（vLLM v0.20.0+）回归约 18%，仍未解决 — #52630。
  • RDNA hybrid-Mamba：回退到 Triton paged attention，长上下文下 decode 性能崩塌；已确定的修复是由 on_gfx12x() 门控的 split-KV decode kernel — #50264。
  • RFC — 自适应 prefill token 预算：提议让 max_num_batched_tokens 能响应压力，而不是对长上下文工作负载保持静态 — #52906。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. 静默输出损坏，DFlash2/DSpark + 前缀缓存（0.30.0/0.31.0，Qwen3.8-27B，TP=1）— 在缓存命中时可复现；0.29.0 通过，MTP 不受影响。尚未关联修复 PR。#60174
  2. Hybrid Mamba/GDN + 前缀缓存 + MTP 仍会损坏输出 — 24 条评论；此前的 issue #43559 已关闭但未修复。修复正在评审：PR #52244 恢复 MTP 下的 GDN 前缀缓存命中（Qwen3.5-122B-A10B）。#53912
  3. CUDA graph 死锁，跨 TP rank 的 fully-sharded fused-MoE LoRA（0.28.0，TP=2/4，35B-A3B MoE + 多个 adapter）— 在并发流量下挂起。#60845
  4. ROCm/gfx942 引擎在 AITER fused MoE 内部停滞（GLM-5.3，TP8，v0.29.0）— 生成从 >2,000 tok/s 变为零且无报错，KV cache 约 20% 满。#57429
  5. Hybrid Mamba2 非确定性，在 mamba_cache_mode="all" + 前缀缓存下 — 相同 batch 输入产生不同输出。#57267
  6. Gemma-4 MTP 投机解码在 CUDA graph capture 期间崩溃 — _suppress_token_ids 是 Python list，而不是 device tensor。#48503
  7. Gemma-4 MoE 初始化挂起和段错误（0.20.x，2× RTX 3090，PCIe，无 NVLink）。#42390
  8. Sparse MLA indexer 在 KV sizing 之后分配 expanded_block_table_buffer — 1M 上下文下约 1 GiB（B200，Model Runner V2，DSA 模型）。#60450
  9. MiniMax-M3（MXFP8）流式工具调用：reasoning 关闭后立即出现空 delta + finish_reason=stop；相同的非流式 payload 成功。#52613
  10. Rust 前端一致性与路由修复：qwen3_xml 工具解析现在与 Python parser 匹配（PR #60136），并且请求移除/中止后的 DP 路由已修正（PR #59631）。

今日关闭：gpt-oss 20B 工具调用 tokenizer bug（Unexpected token 12606 while expecting start token 200006）— #22519，在 39 条评论和 50 👍 后关闭。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 升级前审计前缀缓存。 如果你服务 hybrid Mamba/GDN、Qwen3.8，或任何使用 DFlash/DSpark/MTP 投机解码的模型，前缀缓存目前是正确性风险，而不只是性能调优开关。在 0.30/0.31 上，安全选项是：固定到 0.29.x、禁用前缀缓存，或在 #60174 和 #53912 解决前禁用投机路径。
  • 流式工具调用仍有边缘情况。 MiniMax-M3 流式工具调用失败（#52613）说明 agent loop 中应保留非流式回退路径，或根据预期工具调用输出来校验 finish_reason。长期存在的 gpt-oss 20B 工具调用 tokenizer bug 现已关闭（#22519）。
  • Rust 前端采用者应等待一致性 PR。 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 搭配 --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml 在 #60136 合入前会产生错误输出；#59314 正在添加 per-request metrics（--enable-per-request-metrics），这对网关侧的 SLO 跟踪很有用。
  • LoRA 部署获得真正的正确性修复。 PEFT rank_pattern / alpha_pattern 之前被静默忽略，意味着 per-module adapter 以错误的 scaling 被服务 — 见 PR #59801。如果你提供带 per-module rank 的多租户 adapter，这会影响输出质量，而不只是指标。
  • 本轮硬件选择比往常更重要。 SM120 上的 NVFP4 KV cache 在 prefill 上比 FP8 慢约 1.7–1.8×（#50416），而 SM120 上的 DeepSeek-V4.1 实际上需要 CUDA graphs 才能获得可用的 decode（#56892）。对 AMD 而言，MI355X Qwen3.8 tracker（#57149、#59575）表明 MXFP4 路径正在积极调优 — 预计会有可观的收益以 stacked PR 的形式落地。
